usage: This is the most common way to say "I'm sorry" or "excuse me" in Moroccan Darija. It literally means "forgive me" and the verb must be conjugated to match the gender and number of the person you are addressing. It is highly versatile, used for everything from politely getting someone's attention to offering a sincere apology.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Use this when speaking directly to a female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Use this when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: very sorry
variants.note: Add "bezzaf" (a lot) for a deeper, more sincere apology.

variants.label: formal apology
variants.note: A more formal expression used in professional settings or for serious matters.

responses.english: No worries (literally: the world is peaceful).

examples.english: I'm sorry, I didn't see you.
I'm sorry I'm late (addressing a woman).

examples.arabic: سْمْحُوا لِي بْزَّافْ عْلَى هَادْ لْغَالَطْ.
examples.english: I am very sorry for this mistake (addressing a group).
